stories.title: Clark Leads BMW Championship Final Round at -17 — Five-Shot Lead Heading Into Sunday — Tier 1

CLARK LEADS THE BMW BY FIVE.

-17 after Saturday's 65. Double bogey on 1 — then an eagle + 5 birdies in 8 holes.

McIlroy and Cantlay at -12. Tour Championship spots on the line.

He can do this. He won the U.S. Open from 6 ahead. 🏆

#PGATour #BMWChampionship

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
WYNDHAM CLARK. FIVE. SHOTS. CLEAR.

Opened with a double bogey and still shot 65 at Bellerive.

McIlroy and Cantlay chasing. Top 30 go to East Lake.

Final round. The BMW is happening NOW. 🔥

#PGATour #BMWChampionship #FedExCup

facebook.long_form:
Window: 8:00 AM ET

Wyndham Clark heads into Sunday's final round of the BMW Championship at Bellerive Country Club with a five-shot lead — and a story that tells you everything you need to know about why he might be the most dangerous closer in professional golf. 🏆

Clark shot a 5-under 65 on Saturday to reach 17 under par, five clear of Rory McIlroy and Patrick Cantlay, who are tied at 12 under. The remarkable thing about that 65 is how it started. Clark made a double bogey on the very first hole and then simply refused to let it define his round. He responded with five birdies and an eagle across an eight-hole stretch and then added four more birdies in his first five holes on the back nine. A round that began in disaster became one of the best of his week.

This is not the first time Clark has carried a commanding lead into a final round in 2026. He had a six-shot advantage heading into the final round of the U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills — and won by one. That experience of being hunted and still closing the door matters.

McIlroy and Cantlay are five back. Both are capable of a Sunday charge. With the top 30 advancing to next week's Tour Championship at East Lake, the stakes extend beyond the BMW trophy — for every player on the bubble, this final round carries playoff significance.

Will Clark close it out? His track record this year says yes.

article.headline: Clark Carries Five-Shot Lead Into BMW Championship Final Round

Gina Kim and Yoshida at -13. Six back with 18 to play.

#LPGA #CPKCWomensOpen

SIX-SHOT LEAD. -19 YAMASHITA. FINAL ROUND AT ROYAL MAYFAIR.

The CPKC Women's Open title is hers to lose.

But Edmonton has fallen for 16-year-old Deng shooting 63 on Saturday.

What a tournament this has been. 🏌️‍♀️

#LPGA #CPKCWomensOpen

facebook.long_form:
Window: 10:30 AM ET

Miyu Yamashita is on the verge of her biggest LPGA title yet — and the story at Royal Mayfair Golf Club in Edmonton this week is not just about the Japanese superstar at the top of the leaderboard. 🇨🇦

Yamashita shot a 5-under 65 in Saturday's third round to reach 19 under par, building a six-shot lead over Gina Kim (USA) and Yuri Yoshida (Japan), both at 13 under. Those numbers are formidable. But the conversation in Edmonton is just as much about who is giving the home crowd a reason to cheer.

Sixteen-year-old amateur Deng from Calgary shot the low round of the day on Saturday — a 7-under 63 — to get to 10 under par and position herself inside the top ten. The reception she has received from the Canadian fans has been extraordinary. In a city that absolutely adores golf, Deng has become the feel-good story of the week, and her Sunday round will be one of the most watched of the day.

Brooke Henderson, the Canadian legend and 2025 CPKC champion, is also in the field rooting for the home contingent. Sunday at Royal Mayfair will be emotional regardless of the final result on the leaderboard.

Yamashita leads by six. She has been dominant. But Sunday in Edmonton is going to be special.

stories.title: Rahm Clinches Third Consecutive LIV Golf Individual Season Title — Tier 2

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Jon Rahm. Three straight LIV Golf individual titles.

2024. 2025. 2026. 🏆🏆🏆

Won Hong Kong and Mexico City this year. Built a lead so big he clinched it at a T41 finish.

Rahm: "I can even enjoy not playing good this week. It feels really good."

#LIVGolf #Rahm

facebook.long_form:
Window: 3:30 PM ET

Jon Rahm did not need a great week to win the LIV Golf individual season title for the third consecutive year. He needed the lead he built earlier in 2026 — and that was more than enough.

Rahm clinched the 2026 LIV Golf Individual Championship at Trump National Golf Club Bedminster despite finishing tied for 41st at the LIV New York event, posting an 8-over-par total. In any other season, a performance like that would mean nothing beyond a forgotten leaderboard line. In 2026, Rahm's early-season dominance had built such an insurmountable points advantage that no result at Bedminster could knock him out.

He won LIV Golf Hong Kong and LIV Golf Mexico City this season. In his first six starts of the year, he had two wins, three runner-up finishes, and a fifth — building the kind of cushion that made the eventual clinch almost inevitable.

The $6 million individual championship bonus is the financial reward. The three-peat is the legacy statement. Rahm joined LIV Golf in 2024 and has not let anyone else claim the individual crown since. He was candid about the bittersweet nature of the Bedminster clinch: "I'll try to enjoy the title once I get over how bad I played this week."

Three consecutive individual championships. Three $6 million bonuses. One of the most dominant stretches of consistent excellence in professional golf, whatever tour you follow.

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
FEDEXCUP BUBBLE. FINAL ROUND. BMW CHAMPIONSHIP.

Fowler came in at exactly 30th. Woodland entered at 31st.

Three points between making East Lake and watching from home.

One round of golf is going to decide it. 🎯

#PGATour #FedExCup #BMWChampionship

facebook.long_form:
Window: 1:00 PM ET

For 30 players, Sunday's final round at the BMW Championship at Bellerive Country Club means everything. The top 30 in the FedExCup standings after today advance to the Tour Championship at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta next week. For those outside that line, the season ends when the last putt drops on the 72nd hole.

Rickie Fowler entered the BMW at exactly 30th in the FedExCup standings — the last qualifying spot. He has been the ultimate bubble player all week, needing to at least hold his position against a field of 50 trying to either protect their spot or take his. Gary Woodland came into the event at 31st, just outside the magic number, but strong play over the first three rounds has pushed him inside the bubble line.

Patrick Cantlay, who is simultaneously in Sunday's final group as a contender to win the tournament, also entered the BMW week outside the top 30. His position at -12 alongside McIlroy is likely to resolve both his leaderboard and FedExCup positions simultaneously. Michael Thorbjornsen similarly moved from outside the cutoff line into contention for East Lake through his play this week.

The math is tight. Just a handful of points have separated the 28th through 31st positions at various stages this week. Final positions will recalculate when the last putt falls.

One round. One chance. East Lake or go home.

stories.title: Tour Championship Preview — East Lake Awaits the Top 30 Starting Thursday — Tier 2

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
NEXT WEEK: EAST LAKE.

30 players. $40 million. The Tour Championship.

Scheffler defending. McIlroy chasing a record 4th FedExCup title.

Atlanta, August 27-30. The best field in golf for the biggest prize. 🏆

#PGATour #TourChampionship #FedExCup

facebook.long_form:
Window: 6:00 PM ET

The FedExCup Playoffs reach their conclusion next week. After the dust settles at Bellerive today, 30 players will pack their bags for Atlanta and East Lake Golf Club — home of the Tour Championship, August 27-30. 🏆

The Tour Championship is unlike any other event on the PGA Tour schedule. The 30-player field is the smallest in professional golf's major championship circuit. The $40 million in total prize money makes it one of the richest. And the staggered starting-score format means that the player who arrives in the best FedExCup position starts the tournament closest to winning — creating a unique situation where every shot you hit at the BMW this week is also a shot at a head start at East Lake.

Scottie Scheffler arrives as the defending Tour Championship champion, having won the 2025 event. The World No. 1 and FedExCup points leader enters East Lake as the player to beat in every sense of the phrase. Rory McIlroy is chasing a record fourth FedExCup title — having won in 2016, 2019, and 2022, no player has claimed four. A win at East Lake would put him alone at the top of that list.

Past Tour Championship champions at East Lake have included Viktor Hovland (2024), Rory McIlroy (2023), and Patrick Cantlay (2022). The field that forms today will make the 2026 edition one more chapter in the history of one of American golf's most prestigious events.

East Lake. The best 30 players in professional golf. See you Thursday.
